wingSparSource: Piper J-3 Cub: two solid spruce spars, aluminium ribs, fabric covered (FAA TCDS A-691; Piper J-3 parts catalogue).
wingBreakStationSource: Lift-strut wing attach |y| 3.40 m (133.9 in) from the centreline: our own J-3 model (tools/own_models/build_j3_cub.py Y_ST, traced from the J-3 three-view). Checks: Piper spar drawing 14383 (J-3 to PA-18) puts the strut fitting 121.25 in from the root bolt hole, measured 123.5 front / 122.25 rear in from the spar root end on a PA-18 spar (supercub.org 'Spar Drilling', quoting drawings 14388/14453), plus ~13 in root-end offset (scaled) = 135-136.5 in; the PA-18 Information Manual three-view (p.4) scales to 129-131 in. 3.40 m sits inside that 130-136 in spread.
liftStrutFuselageAttachSource: As j3-cub-like (same airframe, same eye, Spec.SitHighM): build_j3_cub.py F_ST, 0.645 m aft of the wing LE, BL 0.325 m, 1.16 m below the chord line.

mass.massKgSource: THE AEROPLANE AS FLOWN, not the placard. 805 lb = 365.142 kg empty (loading.emptyMassKg: the landplane's published 680 lb plus the 125 lb seaplane exchange) + the reference loading: one 86 kg pilot in the REAR seat, which is where a J-3 is soloed from, and nothing else - the tanks stay at referenceKg 0, and this aeroplane's own certificate is why (see loading.tanks). 365.142 + 86 = 451.142 kg = 994.6 lb, which is 77 % of the 1300 lb this float is certificated to (loading.maxTakeoffMassKg, FAA A-691 Rev 34 section V, Edo 60-1320). It was authored at 589.7 kg - that same 1300 lb gross to within 30 grams, which is how you can tell it was a placard and not an aeroplane. Why massKg has to move with the empty weight: AircraftLoad gives the sim empty + whatever is in the stations, while RigSolver and PracticeScenario (stall, Vy, ROC, cruise) read mass.massKg straight, so authoring the empty weight alone leaves the rig solving one aeroplane and the sim flying another - the same class of mismatch as the fitted-blade propeller behind the fleet-wide hands-off divergence of 2026-11-10, docs/RIGGING.md.
mass.inertiaSource: The 1300 lb inertias (1117 / 1502 / 2252, ixz 40) scaled by the mass ratio 451.142 / 589.7 = 0.76504, which holds the radii of gyration exactly where they were (Rx 0.257, Ry 0.467, Rz 0.445 against b 10.73 m and fuselage 6.83 m) - the Roskam Part V check in docs/NEW-AIRPLANE-PROTOCOL.md, and the only sourced basis the fleet has for an authored inertia. The float installation is unchanged hardware on the same airframe; what moved is the belief about how much airframe there is, not where it is. See j3-cub-like.json's inertiaSource for the alternative derivation that was computed and rejected.

surfaces._airfoilNote: Ty 2026-11-10, told 26 of the 32 types fly their fin on a 2-D section: "All 26, own build". naca0012-like is 6.30/rad and NOTHING on this path applies a finite-span correction - a vStab never goes through FiniteSpanSection - so these fins carried about 69 % too much directional stiffness at small sideslip. fin-lowAR is 3.724/rad, no camber, zero Cm, Cl_max 1.16 held flat from 25 to 30 deg: a low-aspect-ratio plate, which is what a fin is, and what the rudder on this same tail already used. The hStab is deliberately NOT touched - that is the flat-plate fabric-tail question and it is separate.

fuselage.cd0AreaSource: Tuned 2026-11-09 from 1.25 to the owner's own cruise: he sets 2200 rpm on floats and sees about 75 mph indicated. The blade is already fitted (2150 static -> 15.33 deg), so the thrust at 2200 rpm and 75 mph is decided at 848 N; this is the drag that equals it. Cruise is then 49.4 hp, 68 percent of what the C-85 can make at 2200 rpm, against 93 percent before. NOTE: this is LESS than the wheeled Cub's 0.92, and floats cannot be cleaner than a Cub's gear — so the wheeled aeroplane is too draggy too and wants the same treatment, which needs its own datum and a re-rig.

crossflow.stationSource: Measured 2026-11-09 off the type's own three-view lines in tools/own_models/build_j3_cub.py (F_TOP, F_BOT, F_HW), the same tables the visual model is built from. The midline RISES 0.169 m by the fin station, which the constant-section crossflow body could not say at all (CentreZ was zero everywhere) - and an attached propeller wash needs a shape to follow. Owner 2026-11-09: the vortex has a tendency to follow the fuselage, not a rule, so PropJet traces attached and free and blends them.

spinAero.shadowKSource: Geometric helical shadow depth (TailWake.GeometricShadow): the share of dynamic pressure a fully shadowed strip loses. Replaces the Report 648 wake correlation for EVERY surface of this type, and brings in the fuselage's own shadow on the tail and the wings (TailWake.BodyStation). Ty 2026-11-08: "expand the shadow work to all 6 shipping aircraft include the shadow effects of the fuselage on the tail and wing's too". 0.5 is the depth fitted on the Pitts against the owner's spin attitudes on 2026-11-08, and it is a PHYSICAL statement - half the q is gone where a wake fully covers a section - rather than a per-type fudge, so the six carry the same number until a type's own evidence moves it. What differs between types is the geometry, which is the point: the Pitts' cellule shadows itself, the Extra's stabiliser spans well outside its fuselage and is barely shadowed at all (measured in a tumble: tail q 1.00 -> 0.96), and the fuselage's own shadow is what takes the fin in an upright flat spin while leaving it in clear air inverted.
spinAero.controlSpoilerKSource: A deflected control on a BROADSIDE surface acts as a spoiler on the separated wake, not as a flap: adds k*sin(delta)*|sin(alpha_chord)|*q*S normal to the FIXED surface's own plane, over hinged tail strips only, ramped in over 20 deg from controlSpoilerOnsetDeg. 0.6 is the PITTS' value and is carried unchanged, not refitted per type: it was fitted there on 2026-11-10 to Ty flying a clip of his own Pitts flat spin ("the elevator literally does nothing in the spin"), and pitts-s2b-like.json holds the sweep it came from - elevator authority at alpha 80 of 3.7 deg/s2 at k 0, 15.5 at 0.3, 27.4 at 0.6, 43.4 at 1.0, where 1.0 leaves the curve nearly flat from 30 to 90 deg and a plate should not be. WHY THIS TYPE HAS IT NOW. It shipped on the Pitts and the Extra alone, and that was STAGING rather than a finding: the argument for the term is about the SECTION - post-stall the section law is Cd_max*sin(theta), which is flat at broadside, so a strip model gives a control on a broadside surface a direction to point its force in and no magnitude to command - and when this type's horizontal tail became a flat plate on 2026-11-10 (b7396cd0: stall 9 deg, Cl_max 0.90, blend 44) that argument started applying to it too. Worse, the controlSpoilerOnsetDeg 10 that came with the plate was INERT here, because the spoiler block in AeroModel.Compute is gated on controlSpoilerK > 0.0: the onset was moving the start of a term multiplied by zero, and the hole it was meant to close was being closed by the 44 deg blend alone. Ty 2026-11-10, shown exactly that and the argument that the restriction to two types was staging: "Do it". MEASURED ON THIS TYPE (SpoilerFleetProbe, SPOILER_FLEET=1). Authority is the pitching moment the stick's whole travel commands at 30 m/s with the wind turned to the body alpha asked for, as a fraction of its own alpha 0 value; the floor is the worst of it over alpha 10-60 at a 0.5 deg step. Floor 0.110 at alpha 42 -> 0.182 at alpha 28; alpha 45 0.131 -> 0.221. IT COSTS THE PITCH DAMPING NOTHING, and for a mechanical reason rather than a lucky one: the term carries sin(gain*deflEff) and is gated on a non-zero deflection, so it cannot appear in a controls-neutral quantity, and dM/dq is one. VERIFIED rather than asserted, because if it had moved then the gate would not be what we think it is: the worst dM/dq over alpha 10-60 is BIT-IDENTICAL at k 0 and k 0.6 on all eleven configs that gained it and on the two that already had it. Vso AND THE TRIM ARE UNMOVED TOO, which was not obvious and had to be measured rather than argued: unlike stabHighAlphaK's 60-90 deg band, this term opens at 10 deg of the strip's OWN flow, and a tail strip with the stick near its aft stop at the stall is not self-evidently below that. It is - measured on the Stearman at its own Vso, the stabiliser's local angle is 2.74 deg against the 10 deg onset, because the downwash (3.49 deg there) and the stabiliser's own negative incidence take it out of the body alpha - so the ramp never opens in any ordinary flight condition and every type's Vso, trim alpha and trim elevator come out unchanged to the digit. WHAT IT DOES CHANGE is high-alpha pitch authority and therefore the spin, which is the point, and nothing below the ramp.
spinAero.controlSpoilerOnsetDegSource: The spoiler ramp starts at the SECTION'S OWN STALL. 30 deg was chosen when every hStab was a naca0012 (stall 14 deg); a flat plate stalls at 9-12, which left alpha 20-34 with no table effectiveness and no spoiler yet - and that band WAS the hole in the elevator authority. Worth the whole difference: authority floor 0.165 at onset 30 against 0.249 at onset 10. Ty 2026-11-10 accepted the plate knowing this moves the term he judged the Pitts' spin on.

propulsion.dryBoundaryExcessSource: Dry boundary friction excess at rest, over the power curve's own running friction intercept (PistonEngine.BoundaryFrictionFactor): 2.90 means this engine resists 3.90x its running friction when it is dead and dry. Continental C-85, 188 cu in, 4 cyl, CR 6.3, metal propeller. SOLVED 2026-11-10 (lane/claude-boundary-friction, CompressionStopProbe with COMPSTOP=1 SOLVE=1) against Ty's anchor "Cranking resistance should be calibrated such that at fine pitch the prop stops right at level flight stall speed", and then his "fix it per engine": it is the one value that puts the measured stopping speed on this type's OWN stall speed, 19.6 m/s = 44 mph (PracticeScenario.EstimateVso, sea level, flaps up - the number the rest of the suite is tuned against, not a book figure). Solved and not predicted: nothing inside an engine explains the fleet's spread, because motoring friction and rated torque both scale with displacement - see PistonEngine.BoundaryExcessFor for what was tried and rejected. THIS IS NOW THE ONLY THING IN THE DEAD-ENGINE MODEL THAT IS FITTED TO ANYTHING: the compression peak beside it is the engine's own gas load out of its displacement and compression ratio (PistonCompression.PeakNmFor), and the speed a stopped propeller breaks away at is a measurement rather than an anchor. Re-solving moves it about 0.1 because the sweep that measures the stopping speed steps 0.25 m/s. The fleet default for every type not yet solved is 3.0.
propulsion.bladePitchSource: Fitted 2026-11-09 to the owner's OWN aeroplane: 2150 rpm static at full power, sea level, on his metal propeller (he says 76AK; propMaterialSource here says 76AM-2 — worth reconciling). He does not have the wooden blade, so this figure belongs to the FLOAT Cub and not to the wheeled one. Fit: PistonEngine.FitPitchForStaticRpm, blade-element against the engine's torque. Static rpm for any fixed-pitch type with a TCDS is published there; take the middle of the range at sea level.
propulsion.propMaterialSource: Sensenich 76AM-2 forged aluminium: a seaplane flies metal, spray erodes wood
propulsion.propInertiaSource: Propeller + spinner + the crank's rotating parts, kg.m2. From the OWNER'S BLADE RULE (2026-11-09, tools/aircraft_builder/prop_inertia.py): each blade is 15 % of the net propeller weight with its centre of mass at 25 % of the DIAMETER from the axis, the rest being hub near the axis - because a heavy constant-speed hub contributes almost nothing to sum(m r^2), so a mass-weighted estimate overstates the couple. M 20.0 kg, D 1.83 m, 2 blades: blades 1.256 + hub 0.140 (k 0.10 m) + crank 0.05 = 1.45, against 2.4 before. MASS: ESTIMATED: Sensenich 76AM-2 forged aluminium, the Super Cub metal class at 44 lb. Continental A-65/C-85, four small cylinders. VALIDATION: the rule reproduces Hartzell's published two-blade polar moment to +18 % (1.412 against 1.198) and runs +60 % high on their three-blade one, so it is applied to two-blade types only.

floats.incidenceDegSource: Rigged angle, degrees, leading edge up. 6 deg chosen 2026-11-09 to satisfy BOTH of Ty's figures at once: the floats carry their own weight plus some AT STALL (115 percent at 6 deg) and the stall speed is 2-5 percent lower with floats than without (3.5 percent at 6 deg) - his own correction, the lift shows at the stall and not in cruise. Two independent claims, one model, one angle. He will test floats against wheels on the next build and this can be refined then. His friend is Wipaire's chief engineer and test pilot, so the behaviour is measured, not folklore.

loading._cgLimitsSource: FAA AIRCRAFT SPECIFICATION A-691 REV 34 (March 8, 2011), section V, Model J3C-65S, the EDO 60-1320 rows - which is the float this aeroplane wears (docs/models/j3-cub-own-PROVENANCE.md). The certificate gives THREE seaplane grosses by float model: '1160 lb. with McKinley floats / 1200 lb. with Edo, Wollam or Heath floats / 1300 lb. with Edo 60-1320, Edo 92-1400 or Wollam 1200 floats', and the owner 2026-11-11: 'The j3 has several gross weights on floats by serial number and I think the highest is 1300 just use the highest in the tcds.' So maxTakeoffMassKg 589.67 = 1300 lb, and the config's old 589.7 kg massKg was that gross to within 30 grams - it was the placard, not an aeroplane. C.G. Range at that weight is '(+10.6) to (+19.0) with Edo 60-1320 or Wollam 1200 floats and 1300 lb. maximum weight'. THE AFT LIMIT IS 3.7 INCHES TIGHTER THAN THE LANDPLANE'S +22.7, so the landplane's envelope must NOT be copied across. Mapped through the same datum as j3-cub-like (datum = wing leading edge = body x +0.4073, body x = 0.4073 - arm x 0.0254): forward 0.13806 m, aft -0.0753 m. The mapping was verified against this file's own authored arms rather than assumed - they come back as the certificate's own stations to three decimals: seats +9.000 and +36.000, baggage +49.000, fuel -18.000. The authored CG (-0.05, i.e. +18.00) sits 1.0 inch inside the aft limit.
loading._emptyCgCheck: The certificate also gives an EMPTY-weight CG range for this float at 1300 lb with the 'Solo flying in rear seat only' placard: (+8.7) to (+16.8), and it is the sharpest check this config has - it is what decided the reference loading (loading.tanks). The empty CG AircraftLoad solves backwards from mass.cg and the reference stations is body x +0.0264 = +13.77 in, comfortably inside; declaring full tanks in the reference instead would have put it at +16.99, outside. With it where it is, every fuel state is legal: solo in the rear, the CG runs +18.00 with the tanks dry to +15.57 brim-full, against the +10.6 to +19.0 range above, and the nose tank ahead of the datum carries the CG FORWARD as it fills, so running the tanks dry is the aft-critical case - which is exactly what the certificate's placard and its separate empty-weight range are about. The equivalent landplane figures are +13.19 empty and +18.16 to +15.39 loaded, against its wider (+8.5) to (+20.3) and (+10.6) to (+22.7); the landplane is so much more forgiving that it would never have caught a reference loading this type cannot take.
loading._emptyMassKgSource: 805 lb = 365.142 kg. THIS IS NOT AN INDEPENDENT NUMBER: it is j3-cub-like.json's published 680 lb (Piper Service Memo 41) plus 125 lb of seaplane EXCHANGE weight, the owner's own framing - 'Floats use an exchange weight removing landing gear and adding floats' - so the delta is floats-installed MINUS gear-removed, not floats-installed. Edo 1320s run 171-182 lb installed with rigging and the J-3's wheel gear is about 50 lb, which is the 125. Wipaire publish the same figure for their own installations and call it the seaplane exchange weight, and the owner's own earlier estimates (700/825) used the same 125, which is the cross-check that this is the rule he means. So this file's empty weight must stay exactly 56.699 kg above the landplane's: if the two ever drift apart, one of them is wrong. Before this the key was 0, which means DERIVED, and the derivation ran mass.massKg (589.7 kg) minus the 86 kg reference pilot = 503.7 kg = 1110 lb empty. mass.massKg moved with it so empty + reference load still equals the authored mass, which is the invariant AircraftLoad is built on.
loading._comment: seats[].eye is the seated pilot's EYE (owner Ty, approved 2026-10-31), body frame +x fwd, +y right, +z DOWN, measured on extended gear; the Cockpit camera sits exactly there. The PRIMARY seat is first. loading.seats[].station, loading.tanks[] and loading.baggage[] are the arms from docs/pending/loading-arm-estimates.md (Codex lane, 2026-11-01): a published TCDS/POH arm where the row is CONFIRMED, converted to this frame through that aircraft's anchor. maxKg is the published placard where the source gives one. referenceKg is UNCHANGED and still follows the 172's convention, so the reference loading reproduces the authored mass, CG and inertia exactly and nothing moves at spawn. Whether each airframe's authored massKg includes a pilot or fuel is still the open W&B decision in AGENT-LOG NEEDS YOU.
loading._seatPlacardNote: maxKg is a CONVENTIONAL occupant placard (250 lb, and the J-3's own authored 300 lb), not a figure read from a POH. referenceKg follows the 172's convention: the primary seat carries the pilot that mass.massKg already includes, so the reference loading still reproduces the authored mass, CG and inertia exactly and nothing moves at spawn. Whether each airframe's authored massKg really includes a pilot is the open W&B decision in AGENT-LOG NEEDS YOU.

tanks.label: Nose tank
tanks._referenceKgSource: STAYS 0, and THIS aeroplane is the one that proved it. Putting the full 12 gallons (32.71 kg at A-691's -18 in station) into the reference was tried on 2026-11-11 and measured: because AircraftLoad solves the empty CG backwards from mass.cg and the reference stations, it put this file's solved empty CG at +16.99 in, outside A-691's empty-weight CG range for the solo-rear placard on Edo 60-1320 floats (+8.7 to +16.8), and the solo-rear-with-dry-tanks case 1.6 in behind the +19.0 aft limit. The float's aft limit is 3.7 in tighter than the landplane's, so the landplane alone would never have caught it. At referenceKg 0 the empty CG is +13.77 and every fuel state is legal (+18.00 dry to +15.57 full). Full reasoning in j3-cub-like.json's _referenceKgSource.

airspeed._unitsSource: As the landplane J-3: Ty's explicit call; 1938 fabric with a period mph ASI.
airspeed._unitsRule: Ty 2026-11-10, asked what rule the other 27 types follow after settling five by hand, chose "by era and category": "Vintage, fabric and experimental types read mph; anything certified modern or turbine reads knots." FlyingGame.Core.Instruments.AsiUnits carries the rule and the exceptions.
